**Not for frontend use.** Service-to-service, reachable only from inside the internal network — it is deliberately outside the prefix the gateway routes (ADR-0003) and is unauthenticated by design (ADR-0001).

Atomically flips the oldest `pending` process to `processing` (FIFO, `SKIP LOCKED`) and mints its single-use job token, returning the plaintext here and persisting only its SHA-256. The response also carries a time-boxed presigned URL for the PDF and the requirement catalog — the rules in force only; retired requirements never travel here.

info.title: Analisadora API
info.description:
Persistence API for the LicIA Analisadora: procurement processes under AI-assisted compliance analysis.

**Authentication.** This service never validates a JWT (design D5). The Traefik gateway performs forward-auth against the user API and injects the `X-User-*` headers. Through the gateway you therefore present a Bearer token (`bearerAuth`); calling the service directly you present `X-User-Id` (`edgeIdentity`). Which one applies depends on which server you call — OpenAPI cannot bind a scheme to a server, so the two are declared as alternatives.

**The `internal` tag is not for the frontend.** Those endpoints are service-to-service, are not routable through the gateway, and are documented here only for the AI worker that consumes them.

tags.name: internal
tags.description: Service-to-service. Consumed by the FastAPI AI worker over the internal network; unauthenticated by design (ADR-0001) and denied at the gateway edge, so it is not reachable through the public address (ADR-0003). Not for frontend use.

servers.description: Direct, bypassing the gateway (X-User-Id header, no application prefix)

bearer.description: The token issued by the user API. Sent to the **gateway**, which validates it and translates it into the identity headers below. This service never sees it.

edgeIdentity.name: X-User-Id
edgeIdentity.description: The authenticated analyst, injected by Traefik forward-auth. **Never send this header yourself:** the gateway's `strip-identity` middleware erases any client-supplied value before forward-auth sets the real one. It is documented because it is what this service actually requires, and it is what makes "Try it out" work when you call the service directly in development.

message.description: A single message, or one per failed validation rule when the ValidationPipe rejects the request.

code.description: External identifier from the PGE spreadsheet; null for rules born in the UI.

type.description: The PGE's categorisation — the grouping the analysis screen renders. A free string; the value set belongs to the PGE.
